afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 121948
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
1248 PM MST Thu Nov 12 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- High pressure lingering over the area will result in dry and 
  tranquil conditions and above normal temperatures for today.

- A more unsettled pattern develops starting Friday and persist
  well into next week as a series of weather disturbances will 
  bring occasional rain chances and cooling temperatures.
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SATURDAY/... 
Latest objective analysis shows upper-level ridging persisting over 
the Desert Southwest. This will result in another day of dry and 
tranquil conditions with mostly clear skies. Temperatures will once 
again be above normal with afternoon highs topping out in the middle 
80s across much of the lower desert locations. 

By late tonight through early Friday, the overall synoptic pattern 
is expected to shift as an upper-level shortwave trough moves in 
from the eastern Pacific. This troughing feature will result in
increasing moisture levels through Friday morning and afternoon as 
PWATs rise close to 200% of normal. With the increasing moisture, 
rain chances will also be on the increase. Given that much of the
energy associated with this shortwave will remain sequestered 
across far southern AZ into northern Mexico, the greatest shower 
coverage is expected to remain mostly confined across southeastern
AZ with some isolated to widely scattered showers extending into 
central AZ. While most of the shower activity will remain 
relatively light, a few isolated thunderstorms resulting in 
briefly heavier rainfall rates cannot be ruled out given that 
there will be a least a few hundredths J/KG of CAPE present. 
Nevertheless, the activity should be inconsequential with average 
total rainfall accumulations expected to range between a few 
hundredths of an inch across the lower deserts to at most 0.10" 
across the higher terrain areas. 

On the heels of this initial shortwave bypassing to the south, 
another shortwave will quickly move in from the northwest from 
early Saturday morning through Saturday afternoon. This shortwave,
however, will mostly be bypassing to the north. As a result, the 
greater shower coverage will be mostly confined across the AZ High
Country with some of the activity affecting mainly the foothills 
and higher terrain areas north and east of Phoenix metro, with the
lower deserts expected to remain mostly dry with rain chances 
limited to less than 20%. Similar to the Friday system, rainfall 
amounts for the most part will remain light with average amounts 
ranging between 0.10-0.25". As the shortwave quickly exits to the 
east by Saturday evening, rain chances will come to an end. 

With these disturbances moving through the Desert Southwest, 
temperatures Friday and Saturday will be on a cooling trend. 
Afternoon highs on Friday will top out in the mid to upper 70s 
across much of the lower deserts, with a few areas potentially 
reaching 80 degrees across the western deserts. Even cooler 
temperatures in the low to mid 70s are expected on Saturday with 
some areas reaching into upper 70s across the western deserts. 

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/... 
Sunday is slotted to be a down day for shower activity with a 
brief period of shortwave ridging and some slight dry air 
advection from the northwest. This will lead to considerably less 
clouds and virtually no rain chances. Models continue to forecast 
one after another northern Pacific waves being ejected 
southeastward toward the U.S. West Coast with the next potential 
system reaching the California coast early Monday before reaching 
our region Monday night into Tuesday. This may even be followed by
another system during the second half of next week. However, it 
is too early to have any good sense on the track of these systems 
as they could move directly through the Desert Southwest or mostly
miss us to the north, so continued monitoring will be needed. 
NBM/WPC PoPs of 30-70% are still in the forecast for the Tuesday 
disturbance, but that could easily change depending on the 
eventual track. So far, any system that may move through is not 
expected to carry anything more than average moisture, so any 
rainfall amounts are likely to be on the lighter side with no
flooding concerns expected at this time.  

With the aforementioned shortwave ridging briefly moving in 
Sunday, temperatures will slightly warm into the middle to upper 
70s through Monday. A more significant cooling trend is then 
expected by the middle of the week as the series of weather 
systems moving in from the northwest will likely usher in a 
cooler air mass with afternoon highs trending more towards the 
upper 60s to low 70s. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0520Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:
No major aviation weather concerns are expected through the TAF
period under mostly clear skies. Winds will retain an easterly
component overnight and through the day tomorrow. After sunrise
tomorrow morning, marginal breeziness is expected to develop with
gusts reaching into the teens to around 20 kts at all terminals.
This breeziness should persist for a few hours before winds
gradually relax through the afternoon.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No aviation weather concerns are expected over the next 24 hours.
Winds will continue to favor a westerly component at KIPL and a
northerly component at KBLH through tomorrow morning before
settling into more of an easterly component at both terminals by
the afternoon. Speeds should remain aob 7 kt with extended periods
of calm and VRB conditions. Mostly clear skies will continue over
the region before high clouds begin to move in later in the period.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
The dry conditions and above normal temperatures will persist
through the rest of today. A more unsettled weather pattern is
expected to develop starting on Friday and persist well into next
week as a series of weather disturbances moving through the region
will bring occasional rain chances and cooler temperatures. 
Minimum humidity values through today will range between 20-30% 
for the lower deserts to 30-40% for higher terrain areas, while 
overnight recoveries stay good to excellent at 40-70%. Higher 
minimum humidity values above 30% are expected area wide starting
Friday and are expected to remain elevated through much of next 
week. Expect overall light winds today before increasing Friday 
through early Saturday, mainly across the western districts, with 
peak gusts mostly staying under 25-30 mph.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...

Gila: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area through at least early next week due to 
water released from the dam. Water release levels have now risen
to 3000 cfs and are expected to remain at this release level 
through the next several days. This will have the potential to 
flood farm fields and low-water crossings along the river 
downstream from the dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Lojero
LONG TERM...Lojero/Ryan 
AVIATION...Salerno 
FIRE WEATHER...Lojero/Ryan
HYDROLOGY...Lojero
